concepts.def: Net difference between accumulation and ablation over a year.
Inputs of snow and ice (snowfall, avalanching, condensation).
Boundary where accumulation = ablation; rises with climate warming.
Glacier slides on meltwater film; dominates warm-based glaciers.
Plastic flow within ice; dominates cold-based glaciers.

walkthroughs.body_html: Positive balance (accumulation > ablation) drives advance; negative balance triggers retreat. Greenland Ice Sheet lost about 280 Gt/yr (2003-2018). Globally, glaciers lost about 9 trillion tonnes 1961-2016, contributing 27 mm to sea level rise.

Warm-based glaciers in temperate Alps slide on basal meltwater at 50-300 m/yr. Cold-based glaciers in Antarctica move at 1-10 m/yr through internal deformation alone. Surge events can briefly reach 100 m/day.

Greenland outlet glacier doubled flow speed from 6 km/yr (1990s) to over 12 km/yr (2003). Calving front retreated 40 km since 1850. Drains 7 percent of Greenland Ice Sheet, contributing to 4 percent of global sea level rise.
